laws.rule: Table Mountain National Park daily conservation fees, 1 November 2026 to 31 October 2027, international visitors: Cape Point R592 adult (12+), R288 child (2 to 11); Boulders R282 and R138; Newlands, Oudekraal, Silvermine and Tokai R230 and R115. (No RBA rate for ZAR; at the South African Reserve Bank rate of 30 October 2026 crossed via the RBA USD rate of 30 October 2026, A$1 = about 11.7177 ZAR: R592 ≈ A$50.52; R288 ≈ A$24.58; R282 ≈ A$24.07; R138 ≈ A$11.78; R230 ≈ A$19.63; R115 ≈ A$9.81)
Cape Point and Boulders gates are cash-free (cards only); one payment per vehicle at Cape Point. The standard (international) rate is applied unless South African ID is shown.

Cederberg Wilderness Area (CapeNature): no fires (gas cookers included), no pets, no firearms, no picking flowers or collecting seed. There are no rubbish bins or toilets: carry all refuse out and bury waste and toilet paper with a trowel.

layers.process: Cederberg Wilderness Area: a hiking permit is needed for the trails. Day permits are bought at the reserve office or through CapeNature Central Reservations (Wolfberg Arch permits at Sanddrif, Driehoek or Keurbosfontein; Stadsaal Cave and Truitjieskraal at several offices). Overnight hiking permits come from the CapeNature Contact Centre or the Algeria office.
Cederberg Wilderness Area: a minimum of 3 adult hikers is required for any Wilderness Trail, day or overnight (4 to 12 is the ideal group size).

Cederberg overnight Wilderness trails: R200 a person a night (about A$17.07), and wilderness conservation fees also apply. Bouldering permits, same price for local and international climbers: R85 a day (about A$7.25), R140 a weekend (about A$11.95), R280 a week (about A$23.90), R1 015 a month (about A$86.62), R2 400 a season (about A$204.82), R4 795 a year (about A$409.21). The tariff period on CapeNature's page is 1 September 2025 to 31 August 2026, which has ended; check the current sheet. (No RBA rate for ZAR; at the South African Reserve Bank rate of 30 October 2026 crossed via the RBA USD rate of 30 October 2026, A$1 = about 11.7177 ZAR.)

De Hoop Nature Reserve conservation fees as shown on the reserve page: day access R60 an adult (about A$5.12) and R40 a child aged 4 to 17 (about A$3.41). CapeNature's tariff page gives day-visitor fees 'from' R40 and R20 for the 1 September 2025 to 31 August 2026 period, so the figures may have moved; check at booking. (No RBA rate for ZAR; at the South African Reserve Bank rate of 30 October 2026 crossed via the RBA USD rate of 30 October 2026, A$1 = about 11.7177 ZAR.)

De Hoop day hikes: a permit costs R50 an adult (about A$4.27) and R30 a child (about A$2.56), from the reserve office or CapeNature Central Reservations. Whale Trail (55 km, five overnight stops): group bookings of 6 or 12 people, from R3 230 a person plus a R560 portage fee a box. (No RBA rate for ZAR; at the South African Reserve Bank rate of 30 October 2026 crossed via the RBA USD rate of 30 October 2026, A$1 = about 11.7177 ZAR.)
